title: Scheduler & Cadences
markdown:
The scheduler is an asyncio task started in the FastAPI lifespan (`openexecutive.scheduler.runner.run_scheduler`). It polls every 30s and reads due rows from `scheduled_actions` (in `episodic_memory.db`). The due query uses `claim_due_actions`, an UPDATE…RETURNING claim, so each row fires at most once per process — this assumes a single scheduler instance per database. Polls are gated on an active company profile via `_company_profile_active()`; before onboarding, due rows stay `pending`.

### Cadence DSL

`openexecutive.departments.cadence` supports, all in UTC:

- `daily@HH:MM`
- `weekly@DOW@HH:MM` or `weekly@DOW-HH:MM` (DOW is a 3-letter day, e.g. `weekly@thu@09:00`)
- `quarterly@DD-HH:MM`

When a department cadence is due, the runner invokes the `department_check_in` workflow and chains the following occurrence via `cadence.enqueue_next()`. Deleting a department cancels its pending `dept_cadence` rows, and `cancel_orphaned_cadences()` sweeps orphans on boot.

User-created (dynamic) workflows can carry the same cadence DSL. A cadence-enabled definition enqueues a `dynamic_workflow` action (`workflows.dynamic_cadence`); when due, the runner runs the stored `DynamicWorkflow`, DMs the artifact to the definition's `cadence_person_id`, and re-chains the next occurrence. Saving/updating/deleting the definition reconciles its pending `dynamic_workflow` rows.

### Channel routing & nudges

The delivery channel lives on the `scheduled_actions` row (`channel` / `channel_ref`); the runner dispatches through whichever was set at enqueue time — `telegram`, `slack_dm`, `discord_dm`, `email`, or `__internal__` (workflow steps and heartbeats bypass outbound dispatch). The nudge engine (`scheduler.nudge_engine`, default 15 min) scans stalled `awaiting_human` runs, stale commitments, and idle initiatives, then emits `proactive_nudge` rows routed via `people.channel.prefer_channel_for` — honouring each Person's preferred (last-used) channel and availability windows, deferring those outside their window and skipping those with no reachable channel.

### Bounded onboarding ramp drip

Staff onboarding adds the `onboarding_ramp` action kind — the one *self-terminating* recurring action (every other recurring kind chains forever). `staff_onboarding.service.activate_plan` enqueues the first occurrence; on each fire the runner claims the plan's next pre-generated ramp segment via an atomic compare-and-swap on `ramp_next_index` (`store.claim_next_ramp_segment`), DMs it to the hire with `message_person`, and chains the next **business-day** occurrence ONLY while segments remain — then stops. It no-ops unless the plan has a roster `person_id` and generated `ramp_segments`.

### Onboarding orchestration & check-ins

`activate_plan` also enqueues two more kinds (idempotently, via `staff_onboarding.orchestration`):

- `onboarding_kickoff` — one-shot, fires the next tick: a welcome notice to the hire's **department channel only when one is configured** (no accidental broadcast — routed through the privacy-gated, audited `broadcast_tools.post_department_notice`, which applies the same length cap + privacy backstop + audit trail as `send_department_message`, to the first configured Slack/Discord/Telegram channel), plus intro-1:1 nudge DMs to the manager and buddy.
- `onboarding_checkin` — milestone check-ins at **day 7 / 30 / 60 / 90**. Each milestone is its own pre-scheduled row (no self-chaining); milestones already in the past at activation are skipped. On fire it DMs the hire + manager a check-in and advances the plan's phase deterministically (forward-only). Because `wait_for_human` resume is a Phase-7 item, replies aren't auto-resumed — they land in chat, where the Executive's onboarding tools fold them into task/plan progress.

## Client rotation claim pause

The `client_rotation` kind (multi-client practice mode, opt-in via `CLIENT_ROTATION_ENABLED`) adds one loop-level behavior: while a rotation's `.rotation_in_progress` marker exists, the scheduler **skips claiming entirely** for that tick. Rotation switches the live company context between parked clients; claiming during the window would fire the just-activated client's overdue outbound follow-ups from a context nobody is watching. Everything due fires on the first tick after the original client is restored. Stale markers (crash mid-rotation) are reconciled at scheduler startup, and the rotation row is idempotently re-seeded both at boot and after every slot activation (scheduled rows swap with the client). See the Client Companies section for the rotation's full design.

An optional `notion_sync_scan` heartbeat (`NOTION_SYNC_ENABLED`, off by default) incrementally re-indexes Notion pages the workspace integration can see into the isolated `notion_wiki` collection (not COMPANY), reconciles un-shared pages, then chains the next tick.
